sections.theory:
Example 3.18

Fit a Binomial distribution to the following data and compute expected frequencies:

Solution:

First we compute mean of the given frequency distribution

Given that n = 4, N = 150. Now for Binomial distribution \mu=np but here μ is unknown so we replace μ with its estimator \overline{X}.

\overline{X}=\frac{\Sigma fx}{\Sigma f}=\frac{192}{150}=1.28

\therefore\overline{X}=np\quad\Rightarrow 1.28=np

\text{Or } 1.28=4p\quad\Rightarrow p=\frac{1.28}{4}=0.32\quad\therefore q=0.68

The fitted Binomial distribution is:

$p(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix}{}^{4}_{x}C(0.32)^x(0.68)^{4-x}, & x=0,1,2,3,4\\ 0, & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right.$

The expected frequencies are computed as:

sections.title: Example 3.19 — seven coins tossed 128 times

paras.text: Suppose that seven coins are tossed and the number of heads noted. This experiment is repeated 128 times (i) fit a Binomial distribution under the hypothesis that the coins are unbiased. (ii) compute the theoretical frequencies. (iii) find its mean and standard deviation.
